question: Choose the correct past tense: 'She _____ to the cinema last night.'
explanation: <Go> es irregular: la forma de pasado simple es <went>.

question: Which sentence uses the past tense correctly?
explanation: <Buy> es irregular: el pasado simple es <bought>, no <buyed>.

question: Complete: 'They _____ dinner at 7 pm yesterday.'
explanation: El pasado simple de <have> es <had>: <They had dinner>.

question: Which sentence is correct?
explanation: En el pasado simple negativo, se usa <didn't> + la forma base: <didn't go>.

question: Choose the correct present perfect: 'I _____ already eaten lunch.'
explanation: Con <I>, se usa <have> para el presente perfecto: <I have already eaten>.

question: Which is the correct comparative: 'This book is _____ than that one.'
explanation: Los adjetivos largos usan <more> + adjetivo: <more interesting>.

question: Complete: 'My sister is _____ than me.'
explanation: Los adjetivos cortos añaden <-er> para el comparativo: <taller>.

question: Which is correct: 'She has _____ to Paris twice.'
explanation: Presente perfecto de <go/be>: <has been> para expresar experiencia.

question: What does 'nephew' and 'niece' have in common?
options: They are children of your siblings
correct: They are children of your siblings
explanation: Un <nephew> (sobrino) y una <niece> (sobrina) son hijos de tu hermano o hermana.

question: Which word describes a place where you sleep?
explanation: El <bedroom> es la habitación de la casa donde duermes.

question: What does 'prescription' mean in a health context?
options: a doctor's written order for medicine
correct: a doctor's written order for medicine
explanation: Una <prescription> es una orden escrita de un médico para obtener medicamentos.

question: Which word means 'a traditional practice of a group of people'?
explanation: Un <custom> es una práctica o comportamiento tradicional de una cultura.

question: Choose the correct meaning of <download>:
options: to transfer data to your device
correct: to transfer data to your device
explanation: <Download> significa transferir datos de internet a tu dispositivo.

question: Which daily activity do you do first in the morning?
explanation: La primera actividad diaria es <wake up>, es decir, despertarse por la mañana.

question: Choose the correct option: 'I _____ to the gym every Monday.'
explanation: Se usa <go> con lugares: <go to the gym>, <go to school>.

question: Which is correct: 'She _____ tired after work.'
explanation: Se usa <be> (is/am/are) con adjetivos: <She is tired>.

question: What does the phrasal verb 'look after' mean?
explanation: <Look after> significa cuidar de alguien o algo.

question: <come back> — select the right definition:
options: to arrive for the first time
explanation: <Come back> significa regresar a un lugar.

question: Which phrasal verb means 'to enter a vehicle'?
explanation: <Get on> significa subirse a un autobús, tren o avión.

question: What is the meaning of <find out>?
explanation: <Find out> significa descubrir o enterarse de nueva información.

question: Which option describes <throw away>?
explanation: <Throw away> significa desechar algo, tirarlo a la basura.

question: Pick the best definition for <put off>:
explanation: <Put off> significa posponer o aplazar algo para más tarde.

question: What does the idiom 'cost an arm and a leg' mean?
explanation: El modismo <cost an arm and a leg> significa que algo es muy caro.

question: How would you define <once in a blue moon>?
explanation: <Once in a blue moon> significa que algo ocurre muy raramente.

question: <the best of both worlds> is closest in meaning to:
options: having advantages of two different things
correct: having advantages of two different things
explanation: <The best of both worlds> significa disfrutar de las ventajas de dos situaciones diferentes.

question: Select what <speak of the devil> means:
options: the person you were talking about just appeared
correct: the person you were talking about just appeared
explanation: <Speak of the devil> se dice cuando aparece la persona de la que se estaba hablando.

question: The term <bite off more than you can chew> refers to:
options: to take on more than you can handle
correct: to take on more than you can handle
explanation: <Bite off more than you can chew> significa intentar hacer más de lo que se puede manejar.

question: Transform to present perfect: 'She visited London.'
explanation: Presente perfecto con she: <has> + participio pasado: <She has visited>.

question: Transform to negative past: 'They watched the film.'
explanation: Pasado negativo: <didn't> + la forma base: <They didn't watch>.

question: Transform to a question: 'He has finished his homework.'
explanation: Pregunta en presente perfecto: <Has> + sujeto + participio pasado: <Has he finished?>.

question: Transform to comparative: 'This car is fast. That car is faster.'
options: That car is fast than this car
That car is fastest than this car
That car is faster than this car
That car is more fast than this car
correct: That car is faster than this car
explanation: Adjetivos cortos: se añade <-er> + <than>: <faster than>.

question: Transform to past continuous: 'She reads a book.'
explanation: Pasado continuo: <was/were> + verbo-ing: <She was reading>.

question: What noun do we form from 'happy' using a suffix?
explanation: Añadir <-ness> a los adjetivos forma sustantivos: <happy> → <happiness>.

question: Which suffix turns 'move' into a noun?
explanation: Añadir <-ment> a <move> forma el sustantivo <movement>.

question: How do you form the adverb from 'quick'?
explanation: Añadir <-ly> a los adjetivos forma adverbios: <quick> → <quickly>.

question: Which is the correct adverb form of 'careful'?
explanation: Añadir <-ly> a <careful> forma el adverbio <carefully>.

question: Find the error: 'She has went to the shop.'
options: She has gone to the shop
She have went to the shop
She has go to the shop
correct: She has gone to the shop
explanation: El presente perfecto usa el participio pasado: <has gone>, no <has went>.

question: Find the error: 'He is more taller than his brother.'
options: He is more tall than his brother
He is taller than his brother
He is tallest than his brother
correct: He is taller than his brother
explanation: No se usa <more> con comparativos en <-er>. Se usa solo <taller>, no <more taller>.

question: Find the error: 'I didn't saw the movie.'
explanation: Después de <didn't>, se usa la forma base: <didn't see>, no <didn't saw>.

question: Find the error: 'They was playing football yesterday.'
explanation: Con <they>, se usa <were> para el pasado continuo: <They were playing>.
